name: Hawaii
agency: Hawaii Department of Transportation (HDOT); driver licensing is run by the county licensing offices
permitAge: 15 and a half (instruction permit), handbook p. 11 and 13; HRS 286-110

teen.holdPermit: 180 days before a provisional license (handbook p. 13; HRS 286-102.6)
teen.nightLimit: Permit and provisional license, under 18: 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. only with a licensed parent or guardian in the seat beside the driver; provisional exceptions for work (signed employer statement) or a school-authorized activity (signed parent statement) (handbook p. 13-14; HRS 286-102.6, 286-110)
teen.passengerLimit: Provisional license: no more than one person under 18 unless a household member (or household member's foster/hanai child), unless a licensed parent or guardian is along (handbook p. 13; HRS 286-102.6)
teen.phone: All drivers: no use of a mobile electronic device while driving (hand-held). Under 18: no hands-free device either, except a 911 call. Fine $300, $400 in a school zone or construction area (HRS 291C-137).

bac.under21: 0.02 or more is illegal (zero tolerance, handbook p. 56; HRS 291E-64 'measurable amount', defined in HRS 291E-1 as 0.02 or more)

notes: Checked 2026-10-09 against the Hawaii Driver's Manual (English), printing HMG 5/2023 (copyright 1977-2023), digital file dated 2024-07-19. PDF page numbers equal printed page numbers.
HDOT's library page also links files/2026/09/Hawaii-Drivers-Manual_2026_V2.pdf, but that file is the Chuukese manual, not a new English edition.

Knowledge test: 30 questions, offered online in English and Spanish with read-aloud (City & County of Honolulu online learner's permit test page). Pass mark not stated in the handbook or on the official pages reached; left null. In-office test languages not confirmed on official pages (county sites for Kauai, Maui and Hawaii returned 403); Honolulu offers an oral test (phone translation or oral classroom test in English).

exam.languages refers to the Honolulu online test. An official HDOT release (2015, still on hidot.hawaii.gov) says the written test is offered in 14 languages: English, Hawaiian, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Chuukese, Ilocano, Japanese, Korean, Marshallese, Samoan, Spanish, Tagalog, Tongan and Vietnamese; no newer official list found.
Supervised practice hours: the handbook sets no number. A state-certified driver education course (classroom and behind-the-wheel) is required for a provisional license (p. 13).
Provisional license from 16; hold it 6 months before a full license; class 3 license at 17 (handbook p. 12-14).
Permit supervisor: licensed for that vehicle type, at least 21, in the right front seat (handbook p. 11; HRS 286-110).
Phone rules and fines are not in the handbook (p. 58 only advises against phone use); they come from HRS 291C-137.
Move over (HRS 291C-27; handbook p. 29): slow down, move to leave an empty lane if safe; covers police, fire, EMS, ocean safety, tow trucks and some state/county vehicles.

School bus (handbook p. 96; HRS 291C-95): the bus's lane and adjacent lanes stop; on a road divided by a space or barrier, all lanes on the same side as the bus stop and opposite-direction traffic need not.
